header.name: Emerging Memory Devices for Neuromorphic Computing (EMDNC)
header.description: This course provides an in-depth understanding of emerging non-volatile memories—Resistive Random Access Memories (ReRAM), Phase Change RAM (PCRAM), Ferroelectric RAM (FeRAM), and Magnetic RAM (MRAM)—with emphasis on their physical principles, switching mechanisms, and material engineering. It covers charge, spin, and ion transport processes governing device performance and scalability, and explores how these memories enable artificial synapses and neurons for neuromorphic computing.
prerequisites_mandatory: Basic knowledge of semicondcutor physics and devices

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to understand the state-of-the-art memory technologies.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to describe the physical mechanisms of resistive, phase-change, ferroelectric, and magnetic memory devices.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to compare the working principles, advantages, and limitations of different emerging memories.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will understand how emerging memory devices can be integrated and utilized for neuromorphic and in-memory computing applications.

lecture_topics: Static RAM (SRAM) and Dynamic RAM (DRAM) – operation and limitations
Resistive Switching Mechanisms: Filamentary and interface-type switching
oxygen vacancy dynamics, and ion migration
Material Systems for ReRAM: Metal oxides, chalcogenides, and perovskites
electroforming process and compliance current effect
Phase-Change Memory: Principles of amorphous-crystalline transition
Material Systems for PCRAM: Chalcogenide systems (Ge-Sb-Te)
Ferroelectric Memory: Overview of ferroelectric materials
Magnetic Memories: Spin-transfer torque (STT) and spin–orbit torque (SOT) mechanisms
magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) structure and tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) effect
Comparative Analysis of Emerging Memories: Switching energy, endurance, speed, scalability, and retention
artificial neural network and spiking neural network
Artificial Synapses and Neurons with emerging memories: Analog and digital switching behavior

resources.title: Chen, Hutchby, Zhirnov, and Bourianoff: Emerging Nanoelectronic Devices
Betty Prince: Emerging Memories - Technologies and Trends
Abdallah, and Dang: Neuromorphic Computing Principles and Organisation
